How often each R, Python and Stata package is loaded by the code deposited with published papers, at economics and political science journals whose data-and-code policy an editor verifies before publication.

4,565 packages · 13,245 deposits with analyzable code · 75 journal collections.

Why count this way. A metric used to allocate credit is a signal, and a signal is informative in proportion to what it costs to produce. A download is one fetch of a file, which a build server installing on every commit supplies in quantity and a faster release schedule supplies more of. A mention in an article's prose is one sentence. Adding one to a count here takes a paper accepted at a journal that checks its authors' code, with the package loaded in that code.

Scope. Two repositories holding two disciplines: 1,543 deposits from Zenodo's verified economics collections and 12,442 from Harvard Dataverse's political science journals. Counts pool both and usage_by_package.csv carries the split beside every pooled total, since the two are very different sizes.

What changed in this version. Stata commands are resolved against the Stata Journal, the Stata Technical Bulletin and the authors' sites replication code installs from, as well as SSC, so software such as grc1leg and renvars is now counted rather than listed as unresolved. The Stata lexer no longer splits a statement at a newline inside a comment, which had reported command options as commands. Install lines record where they fetch from (mentions.remote, remote_installs.csv), and an R package no registry lists is credited to its code host when the same deposit installs it from one. An egen call counts as a use of the package that ships its function, which credits egenmore for the first time. Every mention has a key of its own. And downloads_vs_use.csv sets each package's validated use beside its registry's download count, from SSC's monthly hits, CRAN's cranlogs and PyPI's top-pypi-packages, which are existing data pinned by date.

What the counts do not show. These counts say a package was loaded by code in the deposit. They do not say the code ran. Authors often leave older scripts in a deposit, and a script can load a package inside a branch that never executes. Whatever an author kept out of the deposit cannot be counted at all. The AEA journals, which deposit on openICPSR, are not included.

Files. usage_by_package.csv is the main table. usage_by_package_year.csv and usage_by_collection.csv give the same counts by deposit year and by journal. unknown_names.csv lists names used in code that resolve to no registry, unfiltered. remote_installs.csv lists what deposits install from outside their language's registry -- a GitHub repository, an author's own site -- and from where. summary.json holds the corpus counts the shares are taken against, and README.md is the data descriptor with column definitions.

The corpus tables. deposits.parquet (one row per deposit, with its journal, year and license), files.parquet (one row per file, with its sha256 and the packages it loads), file_packages.parquet, mentions-*.parquet (one table in 10 files, cut by deposit, which DuckDB and pandas read as one; one row per reference in code, without the code snippet), package_versions.parquet (versions stated in manifests and install calls), environment.parquet (R, Python, Stata and Julia versions and operating systems a deposit states), and package_deposits.parquet (which deposits use each package).

The code itself -- file text and snippets, under each deposit's own license -- is published at huggingface.co/datasets/gojiberries/softverse, with every file linked to this record's tables by sha256.

Stata resolution uses the command-to-package index deposited separately at 10.5281/zenodo.21926099. The most loaded package in this corpus is estout, in 3,835 deposits.

Every page the Bihar State Election Commission's archived 2016 panchayat results form returned, and the validated tables built from them. The form at sec.bihar.gov.in/old-sec/ovc.aspx serves one page per seat behind cascading dropdowns; this deposit holds all 258,742 saved responses covering 258,071 seats across the six offices - ward member, panch, mukhiya, sarpanch, panchayat samiti member and zila parishad member - collected in September 2026, together with the seat frame, the seat-reservation roster PDFs published beside the form, and three tables: 258,095 seats, 644,865 candidate rows and 210,717 winners.

Every candidate row names the page it was read from and that page's SHA-256, so the tables can be rebuilt from the archived pages with no network access. The form states no winner, so winners are derived and the basis is recorded; 402 seats name none. 39,003 seats answer "Record not Found" and are kept and flagged rather than dropped. See README_DATA.md for the audit against independent sources and the known limits.

Sixteen Parquet datasets of Bihar local election seats, seat reservations, candidates and winners. The 2011 collection covers Mukhiya winner reports from 23 districts, plus separate Gaya workbook winners and runner-up records. The 2016 collection covers all six directly elected panchayat offices. The 2021-term collection separates the 2021 general election, 2023/2025 by-elections and undated current-term feeds captured in 2026.

Three source ZIP archives contain only original documents and saved responses used by the processing pipelines. The code archive includes scripts, the dependency lock, dataset manifests and data/PROVENANCE.json, which specifies source origins, collection dates, archive checksums and ordered processing commands. After extracting the code archive, run make fetch-sources YEAR=2011, make parse YEAR=2011 and make verify YEAR=2011; substitute 2016 or 2021 as needed. Geographic intermediates are regenerated offline. Missing captures and unresolved source interpretation are documented rather than filled in. Original PDFs and workbooks are retained whole.

Affidavits, turnout, unused source collections and disposable intermediates are excluded. These are reported source records, not a reconciled statewide longitudinal seat roster. The earlier 2016 deposit, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22852474, remains separately available.

A machine-readable mapping from Stata command names to the packages that provide them, reconstructed from the distribution manifests of the archives Stata's net install reads: the Statistical Software Components (SSC) archive, the Stata Journal, its predecessor the Stata Technical Bulletin, and the authors' own sites that replication code installs from.

14,328 mappings · 5,581 packages · 10,147 user commands, from SSC (4,092 packages), the Stata Journal (913 packages), authors' sites (480 packages), the STB (479 packages). Packages and commands both counted excluding internal helper files.

Why this exists. R has CRAN and Python has PyPI: given an import, you can look up the package. Stata has no equivalent public mapping from a command to its package, which makes Stata code effectively unmeasurable at scale and is a large part of why studies of research software omit it — despite Stata being the language social science replication code uses most. Its software is not informal so much as scattered: several archives, one manifest format, and no index across them.

Method. Every package in these archives ships a .pkg manifest listing the files it distributes. Crawling those manifests yields the command→package mapping, including the many-commands-per-package case a package-name list cannot express: esttab, eststo, estadd and estpost all belong to estout. The authors' sites are those named by net install ..., from(URL) lines in a corpus of social science replication code, so a site no deposit names is not here.

Four caveats, which change how you should use this.

  1. A shipped file is not necessarily a command. An f foo.ado line says a package distributes a file, not that it exposes a user command. is_helper flags internal subroutines.
  2. This is a current snapshot, not a history. A command that was user-written in 2010 and later absorbed into official Stata resolves against its status today, so time-series use will see packages appear to vanish exactly when their commands are absorbed.
  3. A journal package bundles what its example needs. SJ 14-4 st0357, a Cox calibration tool, ships a copy of grc1leg.ado. is_documented is true when the package also ships the command's help file; outside SSC, filter on it.
  4. Ambiguity is preserved, not resolved. 284 commands are claimed by more than one package in the archive that lists them first, and are recorded as such rather than assigned a winner.

The accompanying builtins.json lists official Stata commands, each checked against StataCorp's public help server rather than curated from memory.

See README.md in the deposit for the full data descriptor, column definitions and a worked example.
